data.title: Cattle futures mixed amid positioning, easing import tariffs
data.description:
By Heather Schlitz

Chicago Mercantile Exchange live and feeder cattle futures were mixed on Friday as traders adjusted positions ahead of the weekend and the U.S. Department of Agriculture's cattle on feed report that was released after the market's close.

A weak cash cattle market and U.S. President Donald Trump's announcement that he would temporarily ease U.S. beef tariffs added pressure to the market.

Trump said he would temporarily ease beef tariffs to help lower prices, although U.S. cattle producers warned the move would hurt efforts to rebuild herds and economists said it would have little effect on prices.

Trump will sign an executive order within the next two weeks, expanding by 300,000 metric tons the amount of ground beef that can enter the U.S. with lower import tariffs, the White House said. The order, which will be in effect for 90 days, aims to lower prices as U.S. consumers struggle with grocery bills.

Futures fell immediately following the announcement before later recovering.

CME October live cattle settled 0.075 cent lower to 217.925 cents per pound. CME September feeder cattle futures rose 0.10 cent to 329.025 cents per pound.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture priced choice cuts of boxed beef at $385.69 per hundredweight, down $4.24 from the previous day, and choice cuts fell $2.42 to $361.32 per hundredweight.

Expectations for a phased re-opening of the U.S.-Mexico border to feeder cattle imports has added bearish pressure to feeder cattle futures.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Friday cattle on feed report showed cattle placements were below a range of analyst expectations.

The USDA reported wholesale pork carcass values at $97.96 per hundredweight, up $1.47 from a day earlier.

The most actively traded October lean hog contract (LHV26) settled 0.65 cent higher to 80.875 cents per pound.

data.title: Insteel Industries to Close Facility in Ohio, Cut Up to 65 Roles
data.description:
By Kelly Cloonan

Insteel Industries plans to close a facility in Ohio, cutting up to 65 positions in the process.

The company said Friday it expects to stop operations at its Upper Sandusky, Ohio plant by the end of October and move its manufacturing to its remaining welded wire reinforcement production facilities.

The layoffs would represent about 6.5% of the company's overall workforce, given it had 1,007 employees as of last September, according to its latest annual filing.

The company expects to incur restructuring charges of about $4.6 million related to the closure.

The move aims to align the company's manufacturing footprint with customer demand, boost efficiency and cut costs, Chief Executive H.O. Woltz III said.

"We do not expect this action to affect the Company's revenue," Woltz said.

Write to Kelly Cloonan at kelly.cloonan@wsj.com

data.title: CoVolt Power, Utility-Scale Solar & Storage EPC, Files for NYSE IPO
data.description:
CoVolt Power, a builder of utility-scale solar, battery storage, and high‑voltage grid projects, filed for an initial public offering. The Houston-based company has applied to list on the NYSE under the ticker “KVLT.” Prior to this offering, there has been no public market for its Class A common stock.

Business Description

CoVolt Power is an engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractor focused on utility‑scale solar plants, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and high‑voltage transmission and distribution infrastructure such as substations, switchyards and collector systems. The company combines in‑house engineering, self‑perform construction, and a dedicated high‑voltage platform to deliver large, complex projects on schedule and within budget. It serves independent power producers, developers, utilities, industrials and data center operators across the U.S.

Projects are typically built under limited‑notice‑to‑proceed agreements followed by lump‑sum EPC contracts, allowing early engineering and procurement of long‑lead items to reduce risk and schedule disruptions. CoVolt leverages master supply agreements for key components, maintains a direct‑hire craft model, and can act as engineer of record to streamline design‑to‑field execution. The company reports strong repeat business, a growing data center‑related backlog, and differentiators that include self‑perform capabilities, safety performance, and high‑voltage expertise.

Market Overview

  • Total addressable market: Utility-scale solar and battery storage projects over 200 MWdc projected to grow from $28.5 billion (2026) to $41.9 billion (2031).
  • Market growth: T&D investment expected to rise from $149.7 billion (2026) to $218.5 billion (2031), a 7.9% CAGR.
  • Market position: Recognized as a top 10 U.S. utility‑scale solar builder (2015–2025) with scale and in‑house high‑voltage and engineering capabilities.
  • Key competitors: Kiewit, MasTec, McCarthy, Mortenson, Moss, Primoris, Quanta Services, Rosendin, SOLV Energy; high‑voltage peers include Burns & McDonnell, Black & Veatch, MYR Group, Quanta.
  • Industry trends: U.S. electricity consumption projected to grow 36.9% (2026–2036); interconnection requests more than tripled (2015–2025); rapid data center load growth; increasing on‑site generation and storage.
  • Cost dynamics: LCOE estimates—utility-scale solar with ITC $54.62/MWh; without ITC $70.70/MWh; solar-plus-storage $74.70/MWh vs. CCGT $120.65/MWh.
  • Build outlook: Average 49 GWac of new solar and storage annually (2027–2036), representing ~64% of new U.S. capacity additions.
  • Storage trajectory: Utility-scale battery installations expected to nearly double from 60.0 GWh (2026) to 119.0 GWh (2036).

Operational Metrics

  • Customers: Completed projects for 14 of the top 20 U.S. solar IPPs since 2021; high repeat business
  • Locations: Headquarters in Houston, TX; offices in Chattanooga, TN and Albany, NY; 54,000 sq. ft. equipment yard in Houston
  • Geographic presence: Projects across the United States
  • Partnerships: Master supply agreements for key equipment; registered apprenticeship program supporting ITC labor requirements
  • Orders/GMV: Backlog of $3.6 billion as of June 30, 2026 (85% generation, 13% T&D, 2% standalone storage)
  • Other key metrics: Built 7.3 GWac of generation, ~1.7 GWh of storage, and T&D connecting 26.4 GW; average 2025 project size ~232 MWdc; data center backlog ~$225 million; >90% self‑perform on 2025 project starts; 2025 TRIR 0.66, LTIR 0.07; over five million hours without a lost‑time injury; workforce ~345 professionals and 757 craft as of June 30, 2026

Financials Highlights

  • Revenue (current): $739.4 million (FY 2025)
  • Revenue growth: Up 67% vs. FY 2024
  • Gross profit: $102.3 million (13.8% margin)
  • Operating income: $59.7 million
  • Net income: $60.6 million

Management

  • Robert L. Tabb, President & Chief Executive Officer - Former EVP & CFO at Orion Group Holdings; prior finance roles at Mattress Firm and MXenergy/Constellation; MBA from University of Houston.
  • Ronnie V. Shields, Chief Financial Officer - Previously Chief Accounting Officer at Orion Group Holdings; earlier Director of Accounting at Constellation; BA in Accounting from Texas Southern University.
  • Samuel K. Robison, Chief Legal Officer - Former VP Legal at Technip Energies; earlier roles at The Shaw Group; JD from Chicago‑Kent College of Law; BS in Construction Engineering from Purdue.

IPO Structure

  • Issuer: CoVolt Power, Inc.
  • Filing date: August 21, 2026
  • Proposed ticker: KVLT
  • Exchange: NYSE
  • Lead underwriters: J.P. Morgan; Jefferies; RBC Capital Markets; UBS Investment Bank; KeyBanc Capital Markets; Wolfe | Nomura Alliance; Baird; Needham & Company; Roth Capital Partners
  • Use of proceeds: Purchase Common Units from certain Continuing Equity Owners and contribute the remainder to CoVolt Holdings for general corporate purposes, including working capital, operating expenses, and capital expenditures.

data.title: Justice Department, TikTok Reach $400 Million Settlement Over Children's Privacy Suit
data.description:
By Kelly Cloonan

The Justice Department and TikTok reached a $400 million settlement to resolve allegations the social-media company violated laws meant to protect the online privacy rights of children.

Under the settlement, TikTok will pay $300 million immediately and an additional $100 million after entering an order vacating a prior consent decree against its predecessor Musical.ly, the DOJ said Friday.

The DOJ filed a complaint against TikTok in 2024, alleging it failed to comply with the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act, known as COPPA. The law requires internet companies to notify parents, and obtain their consent, before collecting personal information from children under the age of 13.

Since then, TikTok has rejiggered its ownership, management, compliance functions and privacy practices, and implemented measures aimed at improving its safeguards for younger users, age-related controls and parental oversight, the DOJ said.

The settlement represents one of the largest recoveries ever obtained in a COPPA case, the DOJ said.

TikTok and its Chinese owner ByteDance didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. TikTok has previously said it disagreed with the allegations.

Write to Kelly Cloonan at kelly.cloonan@wsj.com

data.title: Nvidia Reportedly Strikes $7B Licensing And Investment Deal With AI Startup Poolside — NVDA Stock Ends Week 5% Lower
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nvidia is paying $6 billion to license AI models from Poolside and extending employment offers to more than 100 of the startup's workers. 
  • The semiconductor titan injected an extra $1 billion into Poolside, valuing the enterprise at $12 billion before the new funding. 
  • The agreement aligns with Nvidia's broader push to promote open-source artificial intelligence systems and guarantee long-term demand for its hardware.

Semiconductor giant Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) has reached an agreement to license artificial intelligence software from startup Poolside for $6 billion and plans to extend employment opportunities to more than 100 of the firm's staff, according to a report by Bloomberg.

As part of the transaction, Nvidia is also making a separate $1 billion investment in the startup. The fresh funding assigns Poolside a pre-money valuation of $12 billion, and the company is slated to continue operating as an independent entity, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Current investors in Poolside will receive a payout stemming from the funds provided by Nvidia.

Tech newsletter Newcomer originally reported the deal. Representatives at Nvidia and Poolside did not immediately respond to Bloomberg’s requests for comment.

NVDA shares dropped 0.9% on Friday and ended the week about 5% lower.

Broadening Open-Source Capabilities

The agreement highlights an aggressive push by Santa Clara, California-based Nvidia to inject capital into the artificial intelligence sector. As the leading creator of hardware that powers AI workloads, the chipmaker aims to drive wider commercial adoption of the technology to secure sustained market demand for its chips and compute infrastructure.

Nvidia has increasingly targeted open-source AI frameworks that let developers freely adapt and build on existing code-base models. By promoting accessible software, Nvidia hopes to prevent artificial intelligence technology from becoming concentrated among a select few tech conglomerates, while supplementing its own expanding ecosystem of software, data, and models.

Poolside, which maintains a presence in both the United States and Paris, specializes in AI systems designed to automate programming tasks, with a particular focus on defense and public sector software applications.

Navigating Regulatory Scrutiny

The arrangement resembles Nvidia's earlier move to acquire licensing rights from semiconductor startup Groq. In that transaction, Nvidia reportedly spent roughly $20 billion to secure a nonexclusive design license while bringing in the startup's founders and most of its staff.

Such licensing and talent-acquisition deal structures have drawn criticism from lawmakers, who view them as mechanisms designed to sidestep traditional antitrust and regulatory merger reviews.

NVDA Stock: Retail View 

Retail view on Stocktwits was ‘extremely bearish’ with ‘low’ message volumes.

NVDA stock has gained 14.5% year-to-date.

data.title: Top News Today: Stocks Rise as Bond-Yield Volatility Subsides
data.description:
MARKET WRAPS

STOCKS: Stocks rose for the session but major indexes lost ground on the week amid concerns about rising oil prices and Treasury yields.

TREASURYS: Treasury yields rose ahead of inflation data and the Jackson Hole, Wyo., central-banking conference next week.

FOREX: The U.S. dollar ticked down amid concerns about Treasury Department interventions in the bond market.

COMMODITIES: Oil futures rose slightly, completing a 6.9% gain for the week as efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz stalled.

HEADLINES

GM Faces Safety Probe Over Engine-Failure Concerns in Nearly One Million

Vehicles

Federal auto-safety regulators are opening an investigation into

nearly one million General Motors pickup trucks and sport-utility

vehicles after receiving hundreds of reports of engine failures.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said Friday it was

launching the probe into vehicles equipped with a particular GM V-8

engine that had already been the subject of an earlier recall. The

regulator has received nearly 500 complaints alleging engine failure in

vehicles that had already been serviced under recall, including nearly

two dozen that required complete engine replacements.

The regulator's newest probe covers nearly 998,000 vehicles, including

model years 2021 to 2026 of the Cadillac Escalade and Chevrolet

Silverado, two of GM's most profitable models.

Fannie Mae Hit by Turmoil in Senior Ranks as Roughly 12 Executives Are

Let Go

Roughly a dozen high-ranking officials were let go at Fannie Mae this

week, raising concerns about more turmoil at one of the firms that back

major portions of the mortgage market, according to people familiar with

the matter.

Word of the senior departures spread across the industry Friday,

creating worries that Fannie's ability to provide stability to prices and

activity could be hampered.

Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac play a pivotal role by buying up mortgages

and packaging them to sell to investors, guaranteeing the investors

payments even if borrowers default. This empowers U.S. lenders to make

more 30-year fixed-rate mortgages.

BJ's Wholesale Wins Value-Seeking Shoppers With Deals on Gas and

Groceries

BJ's Wholesale Club raised its full-year profit outlook, as lower gas

prices and deals on groceries drew more customers to its warehouses in

the latest quarter.

"Gas prices are about as visible as it gets for consumers," Chief

Executive Bob Eddy said on a call with analysts Friday. "There's a price

on every street corner, and our members know that we offer great value."

Including fuel, comparable-club sales grew nearly 12% in the recent

quarter. Stripping out fuel, comparable sales were up 3.1%, ahead of the

2.6% increase that analysts polled by FactSet expected.

Nvidia in Talks to Invest in Data-Center Power Developer Cloverleaf

Infrastructure

Nvidia is in advanced discussions to make an investment in Cloverleaf

Infrastructure, a company that arranges power for data-center projects,

according to people familiar with the deal.

The transaction could be announced as soon as Friday morning, the

people said. The exact terms of the deal couldn't be immediately learned,

but Nvidia is expected to invest several hundred million dollars, one of

the people said.

In recent months, Cloverleaf had been working with JPMorgan Chase on

strategic options, including a potential sale of the business, according

to people familiar with the deal. Cloverleaf raised $300 million in 2024,

the year it was founded, from energy investors NGP and Sandbrook Capital.

U.S. to Boost Beef Imports to Address High Prices, Trump Says

President Trump announced a plan to temporarily allow more foreign

beef imports into the U.S. without paying higher tariffs, his latest move

aimed at easing a run-up in beef prices for American shoppers.

Trump, in a social-media post on Friday, said the Trump

administration, for the next 90 days, will allow up to 300,000 metric

tons of ground beef to be imported into the U.S. without triggering

higher tariff rates. "We have a commitment that this beef will be sold at

25 percent below current market prices," Trump said.

Reducing beef prices has been a priority for the Trump administration,

which is feeling pressure to convince Americans that it is taking steps

to tame food inflation. Record-high beef prices have been among the most

stubborn sources of food inflation for U.S. consumers over the past year

and a half.

Alfalfa Sprouts Linked to E. Coli, Salmonella Outbreak Across 15 States

An outbreak of E. coli and salmonella linked to alfalfa sprouts has

sickened dozens of people across 15 states, public-health officials said.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Friday urged

consumers not to eat alfalfa sprouts grown by Everything Sprouts and sold

under the Calco and Everything Sprouts brands. Fifty-five people have

been infected with E. coli or salmonella in connection with the outbreak,

the health agency said, including two people who contracted both

pathogens.

No one has died in the outbreak, the CDC said. Four people have been

hospitalized.

ABC Local Station Move Draws FCC Scrutiny

When major broadcast networks decide to move their programming from

one local TV station to another, it rarely attracts the attention of the

federal government.

But ABC's decision to switch stations in St. Louis next month is

getting scrutiny from Federal Communications Chairman Brendan Carr, who

is already engaged in multiple legal battles with the Disney-owned

network.

Carr has made inquiries about the affiliation change from KDNL, the

network's home for more than 30 years, to KMOV, according to people

familiar with the matter. The former is owned by broadcaster Sinclair,

while the latter is operated by rival Gray Media.

TALKING POINT When Your Bumper 401(k) Is a Tax Problem Waiting to Happen

Here's a good question for mid- and late-career workers: Do your traditional 401(k) or IRA accounts hold a large portion of your retirement savings?

If the answer is yes, consider changes.

While these accounts have advantages, they also have drawbacks that could limit flexibility and raise taxes later on. Smart planning now could reduce future trouble, as long as you're careful.

A lot of affluent workers have outsize traditional IRAs and 401(k)s because they had no access to other tax-favored accounts, like Roth 401 (k)s, when they were younger. Meanwhile, contributions to traditional accounts were often tax-deductible and came with a company match. So these accounts seemed-and often were-a better way to save for retirement than a taxable brokerage account.

For such reasons, the dollars in traditional IRAs now far surpass those in Roth IRAs. At the end of 2025, traditional IRAs held about $15 trillion while Roth IRAs held about $2 trillion, according to IRS data and estimates by the Investment Company Institute. (Traditional and Roth IRAs often hold savings rolled over from 401(k) plans.)

Advisers see the imbalance frequently. "When people seek retirement advice, it's often because their traditional IRAs are disproportionately large," says Ed Slott, a CPA who specializes in retirement tax planning.

  • Laura Saunders, The Wall Street Journal

data.title: Grades mixed on first day of volatile roll-trade period
data.description:
U.S. crude grades were mixed on Friday, the first full day of the volatile roll period, and as U.S. energy firms cut the number of active oil and gas rigs for the first time in a month, dealers said.

Prices to roll positions from September to October traded at $1.35 on the first full day of the cash-roll period following the expiration of the August U.S. crude futures contract. Traders use the three-day roll period to square positions, adjust their slates and net out any exposure.

Prices tend to be more volatile during this roll period.

Separately, on Friday, a closely watched report by Baker Hughes showed that U.S. energy firms cut the number of active oil rigs by three this week, marking a slowdown for the first time in a month. Oil rigs are an indicator of future output.

Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump threatened economic sanctions on Iran's trading partners, further raising tensions over Middle East supply disruptions.

Traffic trickled through the Strait of Hormuz with only seven commodity ships sailing through the strait and three exiting on Friday, shipping tracker Kpler's data showed.

The spread between Brent and WTI also widened by 28 cents to last trade at minus $7.23. A wider than $4 discount to Brent makes it more economic for companies to ship oil abroad.

  • Light Louisiana Sweet for October delivery was unchanged at a midpoint of a $3.50 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $3.00 and $4.00 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures ​

  • Mars Sour eased $1 to a midpoint of a $3 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $2.80 and $3.20 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures ​

  • WTI Midland rose 15 cents to a midpoint of an 85-cent premium and was seen bid and offered between a 65-cent and $1.05 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures ​

  • West Texas Sour strengthened $1.52 to a midpoint of a $1.03 discount and was seen bid and offered between a $1.90 and 15-cent a barrel discount to U.S. crude futures ​

  • WTI at East Houston, also known as MEH, traded between a 75-cent and $1.15 a barrel premium to U.S. crude futures

  • ICE Brent October futures rose 61 cents to settle at $94.39 a barrel on Friday​.

  • WTI October crude futures rose 23 cents to settle at $87.06 a barrel on Friday​.

  • The Brent/WTI spread widened 28 cents to last trade at minus $7.23, after hitting a high of minus $6.80 and a low of minus $7.48.

data.title: US Army Collaborating With FedEx Dataworks to Support Logistics Efforts
data.description:
By Stephen Nakrosis

The U.S. Army said it will work with FedEx Dataworks on efforts to modernize its non-tactical logistics networks, supply chain procedures and Organic Industrial Base sites.

Military personnel will collaborate with a FedEx Dataworks-led team of logistics and technology experts under the Army's Strategic Capital Initiative. Through the program, FedEx will use its expertise in large-scale orchestration to help optimize stock levels and demand forecasting, the Army added.

Dave Fitzgerald, deputy undersecretary of the Army, said the imitative is part of the service's plans to transition from a dated supply system to a predictive, intelligent network.

The Army also said integrating automation and technology into its sustainment enterprise is a direct investment in the civilian and military workforce.

An implementation plan for U.S. based sites is expected to be finalized by November.
